dialogue.speaker: Rachel Berry
dialogue.text: Coach Sylvester, New Directions has an official permit for the auditorium until five. Our regional competition is in two days, and I need this stage to rehearse my solo.

dialogue.speaker: Sue Sylvester
dialogue.text: Listen closely, little songbird. Nobody cares about your little singing club. My cheerleaders need this floor for conditioning, so pack up your sheet music and get out.

dialogue.speaker: Santana Lopez
dialogue.text: You heard the coach, Rachel. Take your knee-high socks and your dramatic hand gestures back to the choir room before I toss you out myself.

dialogue.speaker: Sue Sylvester
dialogue.text: That's the spirit, Santana. Remind these vocal losers why you're at the top of the cheerleading pyramid—and remember who keeps you there.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel Berry
dialogue.text: Stop pretending you want us to fail, Santana. If we don't rehearse today, the choir gets shut down, and you lose the only place where people actually let you sing.

dialogue.speaker: Santana Lopez
dialogue.text: Coach, honestly, this floor is too dusty for our routine anyway. Let the desperate choir kids have their little practice—we'll look better on the turf outside.
